name: How close can a rear house addition be to the back fence in my city?

mainEntity.name: How close can I build a rear house addition to the rear property line in Los Angeles or nearby cities, and do setback rules change for one-story versus two-story additions?
mainEntity.text: How close can I build a rear house addition to the rear property line in Los Angeles or nearby cities, and do setback rules change for one-story versus two-story additions?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rear-yard setbacks are one of the first issues to check before drawing plans for a rear-house addition. In Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, Burbank, and North Hollywood, the answer depends on the property’s zoning, lot dimensions, height of the proposed addition, and whether the project is attached to the existing house or built as a separate structure. Two-story additions often trigger more restrictive setbacks, privacy rules, and height limits than single-story additions. A rear addition that seems possible on paper may still fail plan check if it reduces required open space, exceeds lot coverage, or conflicts with side-yard setbacks. Homeowners should verify the exact zoning rules before hiring a designer, because a small adjustment in depth or height can make the difference between approval and redesign. The best next step is to confirm the parcel’s zoning and setbacks first, then design the addition around those limits instead of forcing the plans afterward.
acceptedAnswer.description: Rear setbacks are city- and zone-specific, and two-story additions usually face stricter rear-yard limits than one-story additions. In Los Angeles-area projects, the allowable distance can change based on zoning, lot width, existing nonconforming conditions, and whether the project is an addition, ADU, or remodel.
